h: Cows, Lakes and Getting the Most From Your Slot
p: Five minutes of planning at home makes all the difference. Fill in waivers online, check you've got the right session booked and make sure everyone's wearing clothes they can move in. Grip socks can usually be reused, so stash them in the car for next time. Bring water, a small towel and maybe a spare T-shirt for the hot and sweaty ones.

If you're bringing a mixed-age group, think about which session suits best. Younger kids often do better at quieter times, while teens tend to love the energy of a busy weekend afternoon. Remind everyone about the basic rules: one person per trampoline, no rough play and do what the staff say.

MK has a few well-loved quirks that are worth a look after your session. The Concrete Cows are one of the city's most famous bits of public art, and a photo with them is practically compulsory. Campbell Park, right next to the centre, has sculptures, open lawns and great views.

For more activity, Xscape in central Milton Keynes has a real snow slope, so you can swap the trampolines for skis or a snowboard if you've still got energy to burn. The Milton Keynes Museum near Wolverton is full of nostalgic displays from Victorian times onwards, and the MK Rose in Campbell Park is a peaceful spot for a breather.
